---
title: "Partitioning around medoids (PAM)"
description: "The k-medoids cost: the training individuals act as medoids of the target."
---

The k-medoids cost: the training individuals act as medoids of the target.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | Clustering |
| Direction | Smaller is better |
| Uses a test set | yes |
| Score a given set | `pam_score()` |
| Search with it | `optTrain(method = "PAM")` |

## Definition

$\sum_i \min_{j \in T}\lVert x_{0i} - x_j\rVert$ over target rows $i$. The classical algorithm of Kaufman and Rousseeuw (1990) searches medoids freely; here the search is the exchange search of `optTrain()`.

## Use in TSDFGS

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
pam_score(geno[1:50, ], geno[51:100, ])
```

```{r, eval = TRUE}
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "PAM",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain

# targeted: the test set is known
fit2 <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:300, n.train = 50, test = 301:404,
                  method = "PAM", min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit2$OPTtrain
```

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see [How the scores are computed](methods.html). Use `min.iter` larger than 300 on real data and check `fit$converged`.

## Original work

Kaufman, L., & Rousseeuw, P. J. (1990). *Finding groups in data: an introduction to cluster analysis.* Wiley. <https://doi.org/10.1002/9780470316801>

Fernández-González, J., Akdemir, D., & Isidro y Sánchez, J. (2023). A comparison of methods for training population optimization in genomic selection. *Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 136*, 30. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-023-04265-6>

**Repository or website of the original authors:** Algorithm in textbooks and the R package `cluster` (GPL >= 2).
